boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented UMD rituals, landmarks, and shared campus practices—from Testudo luck to a student-section newspaper stunt.

cards.title: Rub Testudo’s Nose
cards.subtitle: Good-luck ritual at the bronze Testudo by McKeldin Library
cards.notes: Find the bronze Testudo outside McKeldin Library and notice the polished nose. Students rub it for good luck, especially when an exam is looming.
cards.short_summary: A well-worn campus luck ritual centered on UMD’s bronze terrapin mascot.
cards.evidence_claim: UMD identifies rubbing the nose of the bronze Testudo outside McKeldin as its quintessential and most well-known good-luck tradition.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor landmark in front of McKeldin Library; use normal campus access practices.

cards.title: Leave a Finals Offering for Testudo
cards.subtitle: Finals-time ritual at the McKeldin Library Testudo
cards.notes: During finals, look for the offerings left by students at Testudo. Keep the visit respectful and follow any posted campus guidance for the area.
cards.short_summary: Students add small offerings to Testudo during finals in hopes of a good grade.
cards.evidence_claim: UMD states that students began leaving Testudo offerings during finals in the early 1990s, hoping for a good grade.
cards.access_notes: View the outdoor statue near McKeldin Library; do not leave items that create litter or obstruct the site.

cards.title: Watch the Flag Unfurling
cards.subtitle: Maryland state-flag display during football and basketball games
cards.notes: At a game, watch the student sections as two giant pieces of the Maryland flag descend with the historical video and familiar theme music.
cards.short_summary: A coordinated game-day reveal turns two student sections into a Maryland flag display.
cards.evidence_claim: UMD describes a tradition in which two giant pieces of the Maryland state flag are dropped from student sections during football and basketball games.
cards.access_notes: Occurs during select home football and basketball games; ticket and venue rules may apply.

cards.title: Take Graduation Photos at the M
cards.subtitle: The floral M at Campus and Regents drives
cards.notes: If graduating, bring your cap and gown to the floral M for photos. Give other groups room and use the traffic-circle area carefully.
cards.short_summary: Graduating Terps gather at the floral M for a recognizable cap-and-gown photo.
cards.evidence_claim: UMD says graduating Terps flock to the M in caps and gowns for photos, and calls it one of the university’s iconic landmarks.
cards.access_notes: Located in a traffic circle at Campus and Regents drives; use sidewalks and observe traffic safety.

cards.title: Join the Basketball Flash Mob
cards.subtitle: Annual choreographed student-section moment at a home basketball game
cards.notes: If you attend the designated home game, follow the student section’s lead for the choreographed hopping and swaying sequence and venue instructions.
cards.short_summary: One home basketball game each year features a choreographed student-section flash mob.
cards.evidence_claim: UMD reports that students break into a choreographed flash mob at one home basketball game every year.
cards.access_notes: Held at one home basketball game annually; ticketing, seating, and arena rules apply.

cards.entity_name: Reading The Diamondback at Basketball Games
cards.title: Read The Diamondback During Introductions
cards.subtitle: Student-section response to visiting-team announcements
cards.notes: At a basketball game, watch the student section during visiting-team introductions. The long-running routine uses UMD’s student newspaper as the prop.
cards.short_summary: Students conspicuously read or mime-reading the campus newspaper during visitor introductions.
cards.evidence_claim: UMD documents that students have long read, or pretended to read, The Diamondback at basketball games when visiting teams are announced.
cards.access_notes: Observe during a home basketball game and follow arena conduct rules.

cards.title: Spot a Presidential Turtle Pin
cards.subtitle: Terp-spirit lapel-pin practice associated with UMD presidents
cards.notes: Keep an eye out for the turtle lapel pins shared at university events. The design has continued through several presidential administrations.
cards.short_summary: A golden turtle pin became a portable marker of Maryland spirit through presidential gifting.
cards.evidence_claim: UMD says President Darryll J. Pines continues the practice of sharing his turtle-pin version with people he meets.
cards.access_notes: Availability depends on university events and presidential outreach; no public distribution schedule is stated.

cards.title: Work Through the M Book Bucket List
cards.subtitle: Twenty UMD activities tracked through the Alumni Association’s M Book
cards.notes: Pick up or download the current M Book, then log the listed campus activities as you complete them. The program recognizes milestones with commemorative items.
cards.short_summary: A modern M Book turns twenty campus activities into a documented student tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: The UMD Alumni Association says the M Book Bucket List has 20 activities and that completing all 20 earns a Traditions Keeper medallion.
cards.source_title: M Book: A guide to the UMD student experience | University of Maryland Alumni Association
cards.access_notes: Current M Books are distributed at summer orientation and can be picked up at the Alumni Center during its stated business hours.

cards.title: Walk Around the Point of Failure
cards.subtitle: Great Fire memorial circle between Shoemaker and LeFrak halls
cards.notes: Find the marked circle between Shoemaker and LeFrak halls and read its historical context. Campus legend says avoiding its center helps graduation arrive on time.
cards.short_summary: A Great Fire memorial doubles as the setting for a four-year-graduation superstition.
cards.evidence_claim: UMD records the legend that students who step on the Point of Failure’s center will not graduate in four years.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor pavement marker between Shoemaker and LeFrak halls; keep clear of pedestrians.

cards.title: Learn the Maryland Fight Song
cards.subtitle: UMD’s 1941 fight song
cards.notes: Use the university’s lyrics and audio page to learn the fight song, then listen for it as Terps rally around athletic events and campus spirit.
cards.short_summary: The official 1941 fight song gives the recurring “Go Terps” refrain a campus home.
cards.evidence_claim: UMD identifies the Maryland Fight Song as a 1941 work by Ralph Davis ’42, copyrighted by the University of Maryland Student Government Association.
cards.access_notes: Lyrics and an audio player are available on the university page.
